definition: The official QFIC term for the UBC stipend — framed as a return on your ownership stake in the global compute network rather than welfare. The language is deliberate: a dividend implies you already own something, while welfare implies society owes you something.
origin: QFIC corporate communications — the rhetorical rebranding of poverty assistance as property income
example: The QFIC quarterly report calls it a compute dividend. The Shelf calls it not-enough-to-eat.
